text:
marco: Quick announcement — billing will change how we surface minute-level usage on invoices: starting 2026-05-12 invoices will show hourly rollups by default. This is meant to reduce invoice size for high-frequency apps and make CSVs easier to consume. Enforcement (rate limits/quotas) remains per-minute.

sana: Short Q: will customers see different overage numbers because of aggregation?

marco: Overage math is unchanged; we apply the same thresholds but evaluated on hourly buckets. We'll add an extra invoice column called "hour_peak_minute" showing the peak minute within each billed hour for transparency.

billing-bot: RFC published: https://redwood.internal/rfc/invoice-hourly-2026. Key points: 1) default invoice aggregation = hourly; 2) free trial credit protection via smoothing alg; 3) 90-day minute-export available by request.

legal: Flagging contracts that explicitly reference "per-minute line items" — please send a list of impacted customers so we can draft amendments.

support: We'll need an FAQ and a playbook for customers who call about faster-looking credit consumption.

ops: Any infra risk? backfills might cause dashboard lag.

marco: We'll run side-by-side simulations for 21 days starting 2026-04-20 and backfills will be staged on a separate queue to avoid production dashboard impact.

sana: Suggest a 14-day fallback toggle in the Console to revert invoice generation to minute-mode in case of widespread issues.

marco: Good idea. We'll add a revert toggle with audit logs for 14 days post-cutover. Action items: billing + legal to list contracts by 2026-04-10, infra to start sim 2026-04-20, support to draft comms. I'll post a status update after the first simulation run. Thanks everyone. :pray:
